Renamed `totalAmount` → `grossAmount` across both modules. `mvn test` and `npm run build && npm test` both pass.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `api/src/main/java/mn/shop/api/Order.java:15,27` | entity field + `getTotalAmount()` → `getGrossAmount()` |
| `api/src/main/java/mn/shop/api/OrderDto.java:5,8` | record component + call site in `of` |
| `api/src/main/resources/graphql/order.graphqls:4` | schema field |
| `web/src/lib/orders.ts:6,25` | query selection set + `Order` interface |
| `web/src/components/OrderSummary.tsx:4,12` | both read sites |
| `web/src/generated/graphql-generated.ts:11` | generated `Order` type |

Three things worth your attention:

**The GraphQL schema field is a public contract.** Renaming `Order.totalAmount` in `order.graphqls` breaks any client that isn't in this repo. The two modules build separately (per the note in `api/pom.xml`), so nothing would have caught a partial rename — I did both sides, but if there are other consumers you'll want a deprecated alias field rather than a hard rename.

**The JPA column mapping moved.** `Order` is an `@Entity` with no explicit `@Column`, so Hibernate derives the column name from the field: this rename changes it from `total_amount` to `gross_amount`. There are no migrations or schema files in the repo, so I couldn't update one. Against an existing database this needs either an `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN`, or `@Column(name = "total_amount")` on the field to keep the storage name. I didn't add the annotation since you asked for a rename throughout — say the word if you'd rather pin the column.

**I hand-edited a generated file.** `graphql-generated.ts` carries a "do not edit" header and is regenerated from `order.graphqls`. Nothing imports it (`orders.ts` declares its own `Order` interface) and there's no codegen tooling wired into `package.json`, so leaving it would have meant a checked-in artifact contradicting the schema. My edit matches what codegen should emit — drop that hunk and re-run codegen if your pipeline handles it.

I left the one remaining mention, in the `orders.test.ts` header comment (line 9): it's prose about why the test avoids naming the amount field, and it reads as a description of the rename itself rather than a live reference.
